info.title: GramGPT Public API
info.description:
Programmatic access to GramGPT — manage your TG accounts, launch modules
(NeuroCommenting, NeuroChatting, NeuroDialogs, MassReact, MassLooking,
DM/group broadcasters, parsers, warming), and read task progress
from scripts, n8n flows, or Claude.

## Endpoints

- **REST API:** `https://gramgpt.io/api/v1/` — documented below
- **MCP server:** `https://gramgpt.io/mcp/` — same tool surface, MCP protocol

## Authentication

All endpoints take a Bearer token:

```
Authorization: Bearer ggk_live_<your-secret>
```

Create a key from **Settings → API keys** in the panel. Secret is shown
once and never returned again — store it in a password manager or env var.

It is **one key for both REST and MCP**. Up to 10 keys can be live at once
(rotate a secret without downtime), and each key has its own `scope` —
`full`, or `read` (GET endpoints and read-only tools; every other call is
`403 read_only_key`) — and optional `rate_limit_per_min` below the global
limit. Both are set when the key is created or edited; `GET /me` shows them.
The API is in **beta**: tools and fields may still change; the live catalog
is always at `GET /api/v1/tools/`.

Calling tools needs an **active GramGPT subscription** — or, for a
`launch_*` tool, an active entitlement for the module it launches: if you
bought NeuroCommenting you can start it over the API without a subscription.
Reading your profile (`/me`) and account list (`/accounts`) stays available
without either, so you can always check your state.

## MCP (Claude Code / Claude Desktop / any MCP client)

The server speaks Streamable HTTP at `https://gramgpt.io/mcp/` and takes the
same Bearer header.

**Claude Code:**

```
claude mcp add --transport http gramgpt https://gramgpt.io/mcp/ --header "Authorization: Bearer ggk_live_..."
```

**Claude Desktop** (config file only launches local processes — bridge with
`mcp-remote`, needs Node.js), in `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "gramgpt": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://gramgpt.io/mcp/",
               "--header", "Authorization:${GRAMGPT_AUTH}"],
      "env": { "GRAMGPT_AUTH": "Bearer ggk_live_..." }
    }
  }
}
```

**Other clients** (Cursor, n8n, …): server URL `https://gramgpt.io/mcp/` plus
header `Authorization: Bearer ggk_live_...`.

Restart the client — every tool below shows up in its tool list.

## Tool dispatch

All actions go through one universal route:

```
POST /api/v1/tools/{tool_name}/
Authorization: Bearer ggk_live_...
Idempotency-Key: <uuid>          # strongly recommended on POSTs
Content-Type: application/json

{ ... tool-specific JSON input ... }
```

The tools are listed under the **tools** group below. Each one has
its own input schema, billing class, and response envelope.

## Response envelope

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "output": { ... },
  "cost_tokens": 0
}
```

…or on error:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": "...",
  "error_code": "input_invalid",
  "recovery_hint": "re-emit tool_use with valid inputs"
}
```

HTTP status follows `error_code`: 200/202 success, 402 no_subscription,
404 unknown_tool / AccountNotFound / TaskNotFound, 422 input_invalid,
403 hard_forbidden, 409 approval_pending, 429 rate-limited.

## Launch options and live control

Every `launch_*` takes `dry_run` (check config, accounts and proxies without
launching), `skip_unavailable` (run on usable accounts, the rest come back in
`skipped`), `queue_if_busy` (busy accounts → the task waits in status
`waiting` and starts by itself, up to 24 h), `strict_config` (422 on unknown
config keys instead of `ignored_keys`), `tags` / `external_id` (your labels:
`GET /api/v1/tasks/?tag=…&external_id=…`, `/stats/activity/`,
`/history/<module>/`, `task.completed`).

A running DM / group broadcast (`spam_pm`, `group_spammer`) changes without a
restart: `pause_task`, `resume_task`, `update_task`, `add_targets`,
`remove_targets`; other modules answer 409 `not_supported`.
`GET /api/v1/tasks/{id}/` returns `config`, `account_ids`, `tags`, `paused`.
Batch polling: `/tasks/?ids=…`, `/accounts/?ids=…`, `updated_since=<ISO>` on
`/tasks/`, `/accounts/`, `/proxies/`.

What changed in the API: `GET /api/v1/changelog/`.

## Limits

- REST: 100 requests/minute per API key — `429` with `Retry-After`;
  `X-RateLimit-*` headers on every response; `X-RateLimit-Bucket` names the
  window (with separate buckets on: reads 300/min, `launch_*` 60/min).
- MCP: rate-limited per client IP at the gateway. Plan for the same
  ~100 calls/minute per key.
- Billing: paid access covers the API — tool calls are **not** metered per
  token (`cost_tokens` is `0`). Calls you have neither a subscription nor the
  matching module for return `402` (`no_subscription`).
- Async tasks: `launch_*` returns immediately with a `task_id`. Poll
  `/api/v1/tasks/{id}/` or `get_task_progress` — or use a webhook (below).

## Webhooks

Register a public `http(s)` URL with `POST /api/v1/webhooks/` (`{"url": "..."}`).
The response carries a signing `secret` — shown **once**. Up to 20 webhooks;
every one receives every event below, there is no per-event subscription.

Each delivery is a `POST` with a JSON body and headers
`X-GramGPT-Event: <event>`, `X-GramGPT-Event-Id: <uuid>` and
`X-GramGPT-Signature: sha256=<hex>`. Every body also carries `event_id` (same
uuid, identical on redeliveries) — dedupe on it:

| Event | When | Body fields |
|---|---|---|
| `task.completed` | any of your tasks (API or panel) ends: completed / failed / cancelled | `task_id`, `status`, `script_name`, `completed_at` |
| `dm.received` | incoming DM on an account while `launch_neuro_dialogs` runs on it, or a target's reply to a DM broadcast in trigger mode | `account_id`, `peer`, `peer_id`, `message_id`, `text`, `date`; from a broadcast also `task_id`, `username` |
| `keyword.matched` | a message in a watched chat matches your keywords (see below) | `account_id`, `chat`, `keywords`, `text`, `message_id`, `date` |

```json
{"event": "keyword.matched", "account_id": 42, "chat": "BR sellers",
 "keywords": ["mercado livre"], "text": "Alguém vende no Mercado Livre?",
 "message_id": 5512, "date": "2026-09-22T14:03:11+00:00"}
```

Verify the signature over the **raw** body:

```python
import hashlib, hmac

def is_valid(secret: str, raw_body: bytes, signature: str) -> bool:
    expected = "sha256=" + hmac.new(secret.encode(), raw_body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature)
```

Delivery is best-effort: 10 s timeout, redirects are not followed, only `2xx`
counts as delivered. A failed delivery (network error or non-`2xx`) may be
retried with growing pauses — up to 5 attempts within about an hour, same body
and `event_id`; `failure_count` grows once retries are exhausted. Answer `2xx`
quickly and dedupe by `event_id`. `GET /api/v1/webhooks/` shows
`last_status` and `failure_count` per hook. For `task.completed`, reconcile
with `/api/v1/tasks/{id}/` if a delivery was missed.

### Watching chats for keywords

`launch_neuro_chatting` with `reaction_mode: "keywords"`, your `keywords` and
`keyword_alert_only: true` — the accounts join the chats and only report
matches via `keyword.matched`; nothing is posted. Keywords match by topic by
default (`theme_matching_enabled`), so expect some near-matches. The watch
runs until `cancel_task`, or for `duration_minutes` with `work_mode: "time"`.

### NeuroDialogs: per-dialog AI, prompts, handoff

- `set_dialog_ai {account_id, peer, ai_enabled}` — the panel's ✦ button: take one
  dialog away from the AI (`false`) or hand it back. A running task picks it up
  at once. `read_inbox`, `get_dialog` and `/history/neuro-dialogs/` show `ai_enabled`.
- `GET/POST /api/v1/prompts/`, `PATCH /api/v1/prompts/{id}/` — your prompts
  (system ones are read-only). `knowledge_text` sets the knowledge base
  (cut at 30 000 chars). Pass the `id` as the prompt id in `launch_*`.
- Event `ai.handoff` — time for a human: the person asks for a live operator
  (`intent: human`), a call (`call`) or the price (`price`) — keyword match,
  no extra AI call; the bot said a `bot_stop_phrases` farewell (`target_action`);
  a link went out with `stop_after_link_sent` (`link_sent`). Body: `account_id`,
  `peer`, `peer_id`, `intent`, `reason`, `text`, `task_id`; once per dialog and
  intent a day. `dm.received` from NeuroDialogs carries the same `intent` (or null).

**`pm_aggregation_enabled` («PM aggregation»)** — the panel's shared inbox: a
listener keeps a permanent Telegram connection on such an account to collect its
DMs. A second connection on the same session gets it revoked, so `list_accounts`
and `pick_healthy_accounts` skip these accounts, and the API does not switch
aggregation on. To get DMs by webhook, run `launch_neuro_dialogs` (with
`ai_enabled: false` it only collects) and listen to `dm.received`.
**AI Operator** is an internal staff tool, not available to clients.

get.description:
Stream the task's event journal — the same lines the panel renders.

`/history/<module>/` records what the accounts SENT; it stays empty when a
run dies before the first send (a dead proxy, a FloodWait on entry), so an
API client cannot tell "did nothing" from "never got off the ground". This
route exposes the journal behind that: launch, per-target skips, warnings,
pauses, connection errors.

Poll it forward with `after`: each response carries `next_after`, feeding it
back returns only what appeared since. `has_more=true` means the page was
capped by `limit` — call again immediately instead of waiting.

Retention: the journal is a Redis stream that expires 24 h after its LAST
line (every new line pushes the expiry back) and keeps only the newest
10 000 lines per task — on a long, chatty task the oldest lines roll off
before the task ends. A finished task keeps its journal for ~24 h. What
must outlive that is in `result` (GET /tasks/{id}/) and in /history/.
`task_status` tells the poller when to stop.
get.summary: Read a task's live log journal

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Redis stream id to resume from, EXCLUSIVE — pass the `next_after` of the previous call. Omit on the first call to read from the start of the journal.

parameters.name: item_type

get.description:
List / create / delete the caller's webhook endpoints.

Events (body `event`, header X-GramGPT-Event):
- `task.started` — the task began running.
- `task.progress` — at most once a minute per running task: `sent`,
  `errors`, `skipped`, `remaining` (null when the module doesn't report
  totals), `replied` (DM broadcast). sent/errors of DM/group broadcasts come
  from their send history; for other modules `errors` counts error lines of
  the task journal and `sent` is null.
- `task.completed` — terminal status (completed/failed/cancelled) with
  `stop_reason` (raw) and `stop_code` (normalized: completed, cancelled,
  proxy_dead, flood_wait, spamblock, account_frozen, account_banned,
  session_revoked, accounts_busy, no_accounts, no_targets, limit_reached,
  time_expired, worker_restart, error, other) and `error` for failures.
  Task events carry `tags` / `external_id` when the launch set them.
- `dm.received` — incoming DM on an account with NeuroDialogs, a DM
  broadcast listening for replies, or DM aggregation enabled. Fields:
  account_id, peer, peer_id, username, first_name, last_name, message_id,
  text, date, media_type, reply_to_msg_id, task_id (last DM broadcast that
  wrote to this person from this account, else the listening task).
- `dm.sent` — a DM broadcast delivered to a target, or reply_in_dm sent
  (`message_id` for reply_in_dm).
- `keyword.matched` — NeuroChatting reaction_mode='keywords' with
  keyword_alert_only=true.
- `account.status_changed` — account status or spamblock changed:
  old_status, new_status, spamblock, spamblock_until, quarantine_until,
  freeze_until (null when unknown).
- `proxy.status_changed` — `is_working` of a proxy on your accounts flipped
  (checked once a minute).
- `subscription.expiring` — 3 days and 1 day before a subscription/module
  ends.
`events` on create/PATCH picks which ones a URL gets (empty = all). Every
body carries `event_id` (also X-GramGPT-Event-Id) — the same on retries.
Failed deliveries are retried 4 times (1m, 5m, 15m, 40m); the last 7 days of
deliveries are in `GET /webhooks/{id}/deliveries/` (`?failed=1`) and can be
re-sent with `POST /webhooks/{id}/deliveries/{delivery_id}/redeliver/`.
Ownership-scoped by the calling API key's user.

To set EXACT usernames pass username_pool: ["name1", "name2"] — handed out to account_ids in order, one each. Names and bios take the same pools: name_pool: [{"first_name": "...", "last_name": "..."}] (or custom_first_name/custom_last_name for all), bio_pool: ["..."] (or custom_bio for all). Pool order is sequential for usernames and bios, random for names and photos — pass <pool>_distribution: "sequential" to change it. per_account_plan: {"<account_id>": {"name_override": {"first_name": "...", "last_name": "..."}, "bio_override": "..."}} still works for explicit per-account values. appeal_spamblock REQUIRES appeal_text (30..2000 chars) — the free-form text @SpamBot's supervisor reads. The check ops need nothing. set_2fa: {password (>= 8 chars) | auto_generate: true (unique password per account, returned ONCE in generated_passwords), hint, current_password} — with current_password it CHANGES an existing password, without it sets one on accounts that have none (others are skipped). privacy: {settings: {"last_seen" | "phone_number" | "profile_photo" | "forwards" | "calls" | "groups" | "voice_messages": "everyone" | "contacts_only" | "nobody", "mute_notifications": "on" | "off"}}. leave_chats: {leave_type: "groups" | "channels" | "folders", delay_min, delay_max (seconds between leaves)} — leaves ALL chats of that type, not only the ones joined by tasks. reset_sessions needs no config but top-level confirm: true.

unwarmed_pace_factor.description: Auto-throttle for accounts younger than 14 days: the pause between targets is multiplied by this (default 2.0). Pass 1 to disable it and keep the delays exactly as given.

start_at.description: ISO-8601: the task waits until then before the first send.

stop_at.description: ISO-8601: no new targets after it; the task ends.

active_hours_end.description: Working window end hour 1-24, exclusive; 22→6 = overnight.

timezone.description: IANA timezone of the schedule and of the daily plan (default Europe/Moscow).

daily_limit_per_account.description: New targets per account per day. On reaching it the task waits for the next day instead of failing. Replies and followups don't count.

daily_limit_total.description: New targets per day across all accounts of the task.

ramp.description: {start, step_per_day, max}: per-account daily limit = start + step_per_day × account age in days, capped by max.

followups.description: [{after_hours, if: "no_reply", chain}] — nudge those who did not reply, from the same account in the same dialog. after_hours counts from the previous touch, max 47.

chain_variants.description: [{weight, chain}] — A/B test: each target gets one weighted variant; its index (from 0) is in history.variant and in dm.received.variant.

skip_already_messaged.description: Skip targets any of your accounts already messaged (default true).

skip_contacted_days.description: Same dedup limited to the last N days.

notify_on_reply.description: Ping the owner in the GramGPT Telegram bot on a target's first reply.

post.summary: Launch auto-warming module: accounts read dialogs / join channels / scroll feed to simulate organic activity.

config.description: Optional module tuning; extra module keys are accepted (see WarmingConfig). duration_minutes and channels_to_join are top-level inputs above. Pacing is derived from max_actions_per_day and the session length — there is no per-action delay knob (min_delay_seconds/max_delay_seconds are read by no warming code path and were dropped from this schema).

dry_run.description: Validate config, accounts and proxies without launching. Returns what would be dropped (ignored_keys) and which accounts are busy, dead or without a working proxy. Not billed.

skip_unavailable.description: Launch on the usable accounts only; the response lists the rest in `skipped` as {account_id, reason}. reason: busy | no_proxy | proxy_dead | status:<account status>.

queue_if_busy.description: If accounts are busy in other tasks, create the task with status `waiting` instead of a 409; it starts by itself once they are free (checked every minute, gives up after 24 h → status failed, stop_reason queue_timeout). cancel_task works on a waiting task.

strict_config.description: Refuse with 422 invalid_config when `config` has keys the module does not know (default: drop them and list in `ignored_keys`).

tags.description: Your labels for the task; filter with GET /tasks/?tag=.

external_id.description: Your own id for the task; filter with GET /tasks/?external_id=.
